1 The diagram shows the sub-atomic particles in an atom of an element.
(a) (i) Give the name of each of the sub-atomic particles labelled P, Q and R.
(ii) Give the name of the part of the atom labelled S.
(b) Give the name of this element.
(Total for Question 1 = 5 marks)
2 A potassium permanganate crystal is placed in a beaker of water.
After several days a coloured solution forms.
(a) Give the names of the two processes that cause the coloured solution to form.
(b) The formula of potassium permanganate is $ \mathrm{KMnO_{4}} $
(i) How many different types of atom are in $ \mathrm{KMnO_{4}} $?
A 3
B 4
C 6
D 7
(ii) Calculate the relative formula mass $ ( M_{r} ) $ of $ KMnO_{4} $

(c) Potassium permanganate can be used as an oxidising agent. State what is meant by the term oxidising agent.
(Total for Question 2 = 5 marks)
BLANK PAGE
3 This question is about alkanes.
(a) (i) Which of these is the molecular formula of an alkane?
A $ C_{2} H_{5} $
B $ C_{4} H_{10} $
C $ C H_{2} C H_{2} $
D $ C H_{3} C H_{2} C H_{3} $
(ii) Which of these has the same empirical formula and molecular formula?
A $ \mathrm{C H_{2}} $
B $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{6}} $
C $ \mathrm{C_{3} H_{8}} $
D $ \mathrm{C_{4} H_{10}} $
(b) In the presence of ultraviolet radiation, methane reacts with bromine to form bromomethane and hydrogen bromide.
(i) State the name of this type of reaction.
(ii) Give a chemical equation for this reaction.
(c) One mole of an alkane burns completely in oxygen.
The equation represents the reaction.
\mathrm {a l k a n e} + x \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow y \mathrm {C O} _ {2} + z \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}
The numbers x,y and z are used to balance the equation.
(i) The complete combustion of one mole of the alkane produces 220g of carbon dioxide and 108g of water.
Calculate the values of y and z.

[ M _ {\mathrm {r}} \mathrm {o f C O} _ {2} = 4 4 \quad M _ {\mathrm {r}} \mathrm {o f H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} = 1 8 ]
(ii) Determine the molecular formula of the alkane and the value of x.
molecular formula =

4 (a) The diagram represents the structure of copper metal.
Explain three properties of copper that make it a suitable metal to use in electrical wiring.
(b) The diagram shows the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution, using graphite electrodes.
Copper forms at the negative electrode and oxygen forms at the positive electrode.
(i) Give the formula of the copper ion and the formula of the sulfate ion in copper(II) sulfate.
copper ion
sulfate ion
(ii) State what would be seen at the positive electrode.
(iii) Give a test for oxygen.
(iv) Give an ionic half-equation for the formation of oxygen at the positive electrode.
(v) Suggest why the copper(II) sulfate solution contains some $ \mathrm{O H}^{-} $ ions.
(Total for Question 4 = 11 marks)

5 This question is about alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters.
(a) Ethanol can be manufactured by the fermentation of a solution of glucose.
(i) Write a word equation for this reaction.
(ii) State the substance that needs to be added for the reaction to occur.
(iii) State two conditions needed for this reaction.
(b) In the presence of an acid catalyst, ethanoic acid is heated with butanol to form an ester.
(i) Which of these is the formula of the ester?
\mathrm {C H} _ {3} \mathrm {C O O C} _ {3} \mathrm {H} _ {7}
B $ \mathrm{C H_{3} C O O C_{4} H_{9}} $
C $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{5} C O O C_{4} H_{9}} $
D $ \mathrm{C_{3}H_{7}COOC_{2}H_{5}} $
(ii) State how you would know that an ester has formed.
(iii) Give one use of an ester.
(c) Aspirin is a compound used to reduce pain.
Aspirin contains a carboxylic acid functional group and an ester functional group.
(i) State what is meant by the term functional group.
(ii) This is the structural formula of aspirin.
Draw a circle around the carboxylic acid functional group.
(iii) Aspirin has this percentage composition by mass.
C = 60.00 \% \quad H = 4.44 \% \quad O = 35.56 \%

Show by calculation that the empirical formula of aspirin is $ \mathrm{C_{9} H_{8}O_{4}} $

use a measuring cylinder to obtain $ 2 5 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sodium hydroxide solution
transfer the solution to a conical flask
add a few drops of universal indicator to the flask
fill a burette with dilute sulfuric acid and record the initial burette reading
add the acid to the flask, swirling the flask continuously
add the acid slowly near the end-point
record the final burette reading at the end-point
The student repeats the titration until at least two concordant results are obtained.
(a) State what is meant by concordant results.
(b) Explain two improvements to the student's method so that more accurate results are obtained.
(c) The student makes the improvements and repeats the titration.

7 In the presence of an iron catalyst, nitrogen reacts with hydrogen to form ammonia.
The reaction conditions used are a temperature of $ 4 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ and a pressure of 200 atmospheres.
This is the equation for the reaction.
\mathrm {N} _ {2} + 3 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm {N H} _ {3} \quad \Delta H = - 9 2 \mathrm {k J / m o l}
(a) (i) State what the symbol $ \rightleftharpoons $ represents.

(ii) Give the reason for using a catalyst.
(b) (i) The reaction mixture is kept at a pressure of 200 atmospheres, but the temperature is increased to $ 5 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $
Explain the effect of this change on the yield of ammonia at equilibrium.
(ii) The reaction mixture is kept at a temperature of $ 4 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ , but the pressure is increased to 300 atmospheres.
Explain the effect of this change on the yield of ammonia at equilibrium.
(c) Draw an energy level diagram for the reaction between nitrogen and hydrogen Include the reactants, products and $ \Delta H $ in your diagram.
(d) At the start of the reaction, $ 4 8 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of nitrogen is added to $ 1 2 0 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of hydrogen at rtp.

Calculate the volume, in $ \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of ammonia formed from $ 1 2 0 \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ of hydrogen.
